concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers in which two integers are identified when a fixed modulus m divides their difference, giving the residue classes Z/mZ, with division with remainder and modular inverses where they exist.

concepts.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
concepts.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers is the largest positive integer dividing both and is computed by the Euclidean algorithm, with two integers coprime when this divisor is one and a family of integers pairwise coprime when every two members are coprime.

concepts.name: Prime number
concepts.gloss: A prime is a positive integer greater than one whose only positive divisors are one and itself, and every integer greater than one factors uniquely into primes.

concepts.name: Binary field and exclusive or
concepts.gloss: The two-element field {0,1} with addition modulo 2, which on bit strings is bitwise exclusive-or, and multiplication equal to bitwise AND.

concepts.name: Hamming weight
concepts.gloss: The Hamming weight of a binary vector is its number of coordinates equal to one.

concepts.name: Two's-complement representation
concepts.gloss: A signed integer is stored in a fixed number of bits whose leading bit has negative place value, so that negative values are obtained by complementing the bits and adding one.

concepts.name: Positional notation and binary representation
concepts.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a fixed base b, and in base 2 a binary string of length k represents its value with the leftmost bit most significant, with addition propagating carries.

concepts.name: Dyadic rational
concepts.gloss: A dyadic rational is a rational number whose denominator is a power of two, equivalently a number with a finite binary expansion.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: The floor of a real number x, written floor(x), is the greatest integer not exceeding x, and the ceiling, written ceiling(x), is the least integer not less than x.

concepts.name: Binomial coefficient
concepts.gloss: The binomial coefficient C(n,k) is the number of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

concepts.name: Finite sets, subsets and intersections
concepts.gloss: Finite sets with unions, intersections and subsets, where the indicator vector of a subset is the vector with entry one at its elements and zero elsewhere.

concepts.name: Bijection and permutation
concepts.gloss: A bijection between two finite sets is a function that is one-to-one and onto, and a permutation of a set is a bijection from the set to itself.

concepts.name: Cartesian product
concepts.gloss: The Cartesian product of finite sets is the set of ordered tuples whose i-th entry lies in the i-th set, and it is used to index arrays with several coordinates.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order
concepts.gloss: The lexicographic order on tuples compares entries from the first coordinate onward, so the first coordinate is most significant, and row-major order is the lexicographic order of the row and column indices.

concepts.name: Logarithm and exponential function
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm log_2 x, also written lg x, and the natural logarithm ln x are inverse to the powers of 2 and of e, and the exponential function exp(x) = e^x is the inverse of ln.

concepts.name: Limits
concepts.gloss: The limit of a sequence or of a function is the value its terms or outputs approach as the index or input grows without bound or approaches a given point, written lim.

concepts.name: Convergence of sequences and series
concepts.gloss: A sequence converges to a limit when its terms eventually stay arbitrarily close to it, and an infinite series converges when its sequence of partial sums converges.

concepts.name: Basic integrals
concepts.gloss: The definite integral of a continuous function over an interval is the limit of its Riemann sums, and for elementary functions it is computed by finding an antiderivative and applying the fundamental theorem of calculus.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.gloss: The geometric series a^0 + a^1 + ... + a^k equals (a^(k+1) - 1)/(a - 1) when a is not equal to one.

concepts.name: Big-Omega, big-Theta and little-o notation
concepts.gloss: f is Omega(g) when f is at least a constant times g for large inputs, Theta(g) when f is both O(g) and Omega(g), and o(g) when the ratio f/g tends to zero.

concepts.name: Worst-case running time of a Turing machine
concepts.gloss: The worst-case running time of a Turing machine on inputs of length n is the maximum, over all inputs of length n, of the number of steps taken before it halts.

concepts.name: Recurrence relation
concepts.gloss: A recurrence relation defines each term of a sequence in terms of earlier terms, such as T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n, and is solved by unrolling it or by substitution.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication
concepts.gloss: Schoolbook multiplication multiplies two n-digit integers by forming all digit products and adding them with carries, using order n squared digit operations.

concepts.name: Directed graph
concepts.gloss: A directed graph consists of vertices and edges, each edge having a tail vertex and a head vertex, and a network of wires and gates forms such a graph.

concepts.name: Vector space, subspace, basis and dimension
concepts.gloss: A vector space over a field such as R, C or F_2 is a set closed under addition and scalar multiplication, a subspace is a subset that is itself a vector space, a basis is a linearly independent spanning set, and the dimension is the number of vectors in a basis.

concepts.name: Linear map and matrix
concepts.gloss: A linear map preserves addition and scalar multiplication and is represented by a matrix relative to chosen bases, the matrix being invertible when it has an inverse and its transpose swapping rows and columns.

concepts.name: Matrix rank
concepts.gloss: The rank of a matrix is the dimension of its column space, equal to its maximum number of linearly independent columns and to its number of pivots after row reduction.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination and triangular matrices
concepts.gloss: Gaussian elimination reduces a matrix to echelon form by elementary row operations, and a triangular matrix has all entries vanishing on one side of its diagonal.

concepts.name: Dot product and orthogonal complement
concepts.gloss: The dot product of two vectors is the sum of products of their corresponding coordinates, and the orthogonal complement of a subspace U is the set of vectors whose dot product with every vector of U is zero.

concepts.name: Vector norm and maximum norm
concepts.gloss: A norm assigns each vector a nonnegative length satisfying the triangle inequality, and the maximum norm of a vector is the largest absolute value of its coordinates.

concepts.name: Complex conjugate, modulus and polar form
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
concepts.gloss: For a complex number a + ib, its conjugate is a - ib, its modulus is the square root of a^2 + b^2, and Euler's formula writes a number of modulus r and argument theta as r(cos theta + i sin theta) = r e^(i theta).

concepts.name: Tensor product
concepts.gloss: The tensor product V ⊗ W of vector spaces is the space spanned by pairs of basis vectors, and the tensor product of linear maps acts on each factor separately, so one-dimensional operations on several coordinates combine into one operation on the product space.

evidence.quote: An empty tensor product is the one-dimensional ground field
The intended operation is the tensor product

concepts.name: Operator norm of a linear map
concepts.gloss: The operator norm of a linear map T is the largest factor by which T stretches a vector, the supremum of ‖Tv‖ over all vectors v with ‖v‖ ≤ 1, for a chosen vector norm.

concepts.name: Order of an element
concepts.gloss: The order of an element x of a multiplicative group is the least positive integer k with x^k equal to the identity, when such k exists.

evidence.quote: the image of $x$ has order $S$

concepts.name: Quotient ring by several relations
concepts.gloss: The quotient ring of a polynomial ring by several relations is the ring obtained by identifying two polynomials whenever their difference lies in the ideal generated by those relations.

concepts.name: Source, sink and terminal of a network
aliases: source and sink of the network
concepts.gloss: A source or sink of a linear network is an end vertex of a wire, where data enter the network or leave it, and the terminals are the sources and sinks at which the network meets its banks of values.

address-shear.name: first address field

address-shear.name: second address field
address-shear.meaning: The second address field, a vector whose entries lie in the residue ring Z/qZ, which the shear leaves unchanged.
address-shear.quote: Write $H$ for the first address field and $D$ for the second, each a vector whose entries lie in a common residue ring $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$, the integers modulo a fixed modulus $q$.

address-shear.name: modulus
address-shear.meaning: The fixed modulus q, whose residue ring Z/qZ contains the entries of H and D.
address-shear.quote: Write $H$ for the first address field and $D$ for the second, each a vector whose entries lie in a common residue ring $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$, the integers modulo a fixed modulus $q$.

bluestein.name: chirp value
bluestein.meaning: The chirp value $\chi_\alpha=\exp(-\pi i \alpha^2/q)$ at an integer $\alpha$.
bluestein.quote: Let $\chi_\alpha=\exp(-\pi i \alpha^2/q)$ be the chirp value at an integer $\alpha$, the chirp index here.

bluestein.name: chirp index
bluestein.meaning: An integer at which a chirp or phase value is evaluated.
bluestein.quote: Let $\chi_\alpha=\exp(-\pi i \alpha^2/q)$ be the chirp value at an integer $\alpha$, the chirp index here.

bluestein.name: phase twist
bluestein.meaning: The phase factor $\tau_\alpha=\exp(\pi i \alpha/q)$ at an integer $\alpha$, which changes sign when $\alpha$ increases by $q$.

butterfly-layer.name: simultaneous butterfly layer
butterfly-layer.meaning: The map that applies the two-point butterfly $H_0$ to the selected bit of each of the $d$ chunks at once.
butterfly-layer.quote: Here $d$ is the number of chunks, not the number of axes used on the transform page, and the layer is written $B_d$.

butterfly-layer.name: chunk count
butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of address chunks the layer acts on, which counts the chunks, not the axes of the transform.
butterfly-layer.quote: Here $d$ is the number of chunks, not the number of axes used on the transform page, and the layer is written $B_d$.

butterfly-layer.name: record length
butterfly-layer.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record stored at an address.
butterfly-layer.quote: Each address holds a polynomial record of $M$ complex coefficients; $M$ is the number of complex coefficients in a record.

butterfly-layer.name: layer exponent
butterfly-layer.meaning: A fixed exponent below 1 that sets the cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ of the layer.

crt-axis-map.name: coefficient index
crt-axis-map.meaning: The position of a coefficient in the list, running from 0 to S minus 1.
crt-axis-map.quote: For a coefficient index $\iota$ with $0\le\iota<S$ (the position of a coefficient in the list), $\Phi(x^\iota)=\prod_\alpha x_\alpha^{\mu_\alpha\iota}$ is a monomial whose exponent on $x_\alpha$ is $b_\alpha$, where $0\le b_\alpha<s_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha\equiv\mu_\alpha\iota\pmod{s_\alpha}$.

crt-axis-map.name: axis index
crt-axis-map.meaning: An axis index running from 1 to d, giving the position of an axis.
crt-axis-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ running from $1$ to $d$ as axis indices (not list positions), and let $s_\alpha$ be the length of axis $\alpha$, with $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ pairwise coprime.

crt-axis-map.name: second axis index
crt-axis-map.meaning: A second axis index running from 1 to d, distinct from the digit width of earlier pages.
crt-axis-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ running from $1$ to $d$ as axis indices (not list positions), and let $s_\alpha$ be the length of axis $\alpha$, with $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ pairwise coprime.

crt-axis-map.name: axis length
crt-axis-map.meaning: The number of entries along axis alpha, a positive integer.
crt-axis-map.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, with $\alpha$ and $\beta$ running from $1$ to $d$ as axis indices (not list positions), and let $s_\alpha$ be the length of axis $\alpha$, with $s_1,\ldots,s_d$ pairwise coprime.

crt-axis-map.name: axis variable
crt-axis-map.meaning: The formal variable of axis alpha, whose powers index the entries along that axis.
crt-axis-map.quote: Let $x_\alpha$ be the variable of axis $\alpha$, and let $\mathcal R=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/(x_1^{s_1}-1,\ldots,x_d^{s_d}-1)$ be the target ring.

crt-axis-map.name: target ring
crt-axis-map.meaning: The quotient ring of polynomials in the axis variables that is the target of the axis map.
crt-axis-map.quote: Let $x_\alpha$ be the variable of axis $\alpha$, and let $\mathcal R=\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_d]/(x_1^{s_1}-1,\ldots,x_d^{s_d}-1)$ be the target ring.

crt-axis-map.name: earlier length product
crt-axis-map.meaning: The product of the lengths of the axes before axis alpha.

crt-axis-map.meaning: The algebra map sending x to the product of the axis variables raised to the powers mu_alpha.

crt-axis-map.name: image exponent
crt-axis-map.meaning: The exponent on axis alpha of the monomial to which the coefficient at index iota is sent, between 0 and s_alpha minus 1.
crt-axis-map.quote: For a coefficient index $\iota$ with $0\le\iota<S$ (the position of a coefficient in the list), $\Phi(x^\iota)=\prod_\alpha x_\alpha^{\mu_\alpha\iota}$ is a monomial whose exponent on $x_\alpha$ is $b_\alpha$, where $0\le b_\alpha<s_\alpha$ and $b_\alpha\equiv\mu_\alpha\iota\pmod{s_\alpha}$.

crt-axis-map.name: axis digit
crt-axis-map.meaning: The digit of the coefficient index on axis beta, an integer from 0 to s_beta minus 1.
crt-axis-map.quote: Each $\iota$ has a unique expansion $\iota=\sum_{\beta=1}^d\delta_\beta P_\beta$ with $0\le\delta_\beta<s_\beta$. Here $\delta_\beta$ is the digit of $\iota$ on axis $\beta$, and $\delta_\alpha$ means the same with $\alpha$ in place of $\beta$.

cyclic-convolution.name: formal variable
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The formal variable whose powers index the coefficients of a list.

cyclic-convolution.name: first index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: An index into the first list, running over 0 to S-1.

cyclic-convolution.name: second index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: An index into the second list, running over 0 to S-1.

cyclic-convolution.name: output index
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The index of an output coefficient c_k, running over 0 to S-1.

cyclic-convolution.name: first coefficient list
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The first input list, whose i-th coefficient is a_i.

cyclic-convolution.name: second coefficient list
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The second input list, whose j-th coefficient is b_j.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Write the first list as $a(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{S-1} a_i x^i$ and the second as $b(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{S-1} b_j x^j$, with complex coefficients.

cyclic-convolution.name: cyclic convolution
cyclic-convolution.meaning: The cyclic convolution of a and b, a list of S coefficients.
cyclic-convolution.quote: Let $c=a\ast b$ be the cyclic convolution of $a$ and $b$, a list of $S$ coefficients.

exact-recovery.name: position count

exact-recovery.name: carry into a position
exact-recovery.meaning: The carry added to the coefficient at position k, which is passed up from position k-1.
exact-recovery.quote: Let $\sigma_k$ be the carry into position $k$, with $\sigma_0=0$.

exact-recovery.name: radix digit
exact-recovery.meaning: The k-th radix-2^b digit of the exact product, an integer in {0,...,2^b-1}.

fixed-tape-model.name: input length in bits

fourier-transform.name: input vector
fourier-transform.meaning: The complex vector of length $q$ that the transform acts on.
fourier-transform.quote: Let $u=(u_0,\dots,u_{q-1})$ be a complex vector of length $q$, where $q$ is the number of entries of $u$.

fourier-transform.quote: Let $\omega=\exp(-2\pi i/q)$ be a [primitive $q$-th root of unity](roots-of-unity.md), so $\omega^q=1$ and no smaller positive power of $\omega$ equals $1$.

fourier-transform.name: output index
fourier-transform.meaning: The index of an entry of $\hat u$, running from $0$ to $q-1$.
fourier-transform.quote: The transform of $u$, written $\hat u$, has entries $\hat u_k$, where $j$ indexes the entries of $u$ and $k$ indexes those of $\hat u$, each from $0$ to $q-1$, given by

fourier-transform.name: second summation index
fourier-transform.meaning: The index running over the entries of $b$ in the convolution sum and the product display.
fourier-transform.quote: Let $c$ be their cyclic convolution, $c_l=\sum_{j+r\equiv l\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)}a_j b_r$, where $r$ indexes the entries of $b$ and $l$ indexes the entries of $c$.

fourier-transform.name: convolution output index
fourier-transform.meaning: The index of an entry of the cyclic convolution $c$, running over the entries of $c$.
fourier-transform.quote: Let $c$ be their cyclic convolution, $c_l=\sum_{j+r\equiv l\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)}a_j b_r$, where $r$ indexes the entries of $b$ and $l$ indexes the entries of $c$.

fourier-transform.name: operation count
fourier-transform.meaning: The number of operations the FFT uses on a vector of length $q$, so $N(q)$ counts them.
fourier-transform.quote: Let $N(q)$ count the operations on length $q$; splitting gives $N(q)=2N(q/2)+O(q)$, which solves to $O(q\log q)$.

frame.name: vertex frame
frame.meaning: The frame of vertex $w$, an invertible linear operator on the arrays indexed by the common address set.
frame.quote: For a vertex $w$, $D_w$ denotes its frame: an invertible linear operator on the space of arrays indexed by the common address set, the fixed finite set of positions that every role's array is indexed by.

frame.name: tail vertex
frame.meaning: A vertex of the network, at which the frame $D_w$ is attached.
frame.quote: For a vertex $w$, $D_w$ denotes its frame: an invertible linear operator on the space of arrays indexed by the common address set, the fixed finite set of positions that every role's array is indexed by.

frame.name: head vertex
frame.meaning: The vertex at which an edge from $w$ ends.
frame.quote: Along an edge from a tail vertex $w$ to a head vertex $q$, the frame change $D_q D_w^{-1}$ converts the stored form at $w$ into the stored form at $q$.

frame.name: logical array
frame.meaning: The array on a wire before the frame is applied, the logical content the stored array encodes.
frame.quote: If $g$ is the logical array on a wire at $w$, the stored array there is $D_w g$.

frame.name: gate input count
frame.meaning: The number of input arrays a gate combines, counting the inputs of a gate.
frame.quote: Here $t$ counts the inputs of a gate, $j$ indexes them, and $c_j$ is a fixed scalar.

frame.name: input index
frame.meaning: The position of an input of a gate among its $t$ inputs.
frame.quote: Here $t$ counts the inputs of a gate, $j$ indexes them, and $c_j$ is a fixed scalar.

frame.name: input coefficient
frame.meaning: The fixed scalar by which a gate multiplies its $j$-th input.
frame.quote: Here $t$ counts the inputs of a gate, $j$ indexes them, and $c_j$ is a fixed scalar.

frame.name: pointwise linear gate
frame.meaning: A gate that outputs, at every address, a fixed linear combination of its input arrays.
frame.quote: A pointwise linear gate $G$ at vertex $w$ with input arrays $g_1,\ldots,g_t$ outputs $\sum_{j=1}^{t} c_j g_j$ at every address.

frame.name: route vertex
frame.meaning: The $l$-th vertex along a route, from the source $s_0$ to the sink $s_r$.
frame.quote: A route is a chain of vertices $s_0,\ldots,s_r$ with an edge from each $s_{l-1}$ to $s_l$, where $r$ counts the edges and $l$ indexes them; $s_0$ is a source and $s_r$ a sink.

frame.name: route edge count
frame.meaning: The number of edges in a route, one fewer than the number of its vertices.
frame.quote: A route is a chain of vertices $s_0,\ldots,s_r$ with an edge from each $s_{l-1}$ to $s_l$, where $r$ counts the edges and $l$ indexes them; $s_0$ is a source and $s_r$ a sink.

frame.name: edge index
frame.meaning: The position of an edge along a route, counted from 1.
frame.quote: A route is a chain of vertices $s_0,\ldots,s_r$ with an edge from each $s_{l-1}$ to $s_l$, where $r$ counts the edges and $l$ indexes them; $s_0$ is a source and $s_r$ a sink.

gaussian-dyadic.name: Gaussian dyadic number
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: A complex number whose real and imaginary parts are both dyadic rationals.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: A Gaussian dyadic number is a complex number $z = a + bi$ whose real part $a$ and imaginary part $b$ are both dyadic rationals, that is, rationals $m/2^k$ with $m$ an integer and $k \ge 0$.

gaussian-dyadic.name: real part
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The real part of the Gaussian dyadic number $z$, a dyadic rational.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: A Gaussian dyadic number is a complex number $z = a + bi$ whose real part $a$ and imaginary part $b$ are both dyadic rationals, that is, rationals $m/2^k$ with $m$ an integer and $k \ge 0$.

gaussian-dyadic.name: imaginary part
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The imaginary part of the Gaussian dyadic number $z$, a dyadic rational.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: A Gaussian dyadic number is a complex number $z = a + bi$ whose real part $a$ and imaginary part $b$ are both dyadic rationals, that is, rationals $m/2^k$ with $m$ an integer and $k \ge 0$.

gaussian-dyadic.name: integer numerator
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The integer numerator of a dyadic rational written as $m/2^k$.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: A Gaussian dyadic number is a complex number $z = a + bi$ whose real part $a$ and imaginary part $b$ are both dyadic rationals, that is, rationals $m/2^k$ with $m$ an integer and $k \ge 0$.

gaussian-dyadic.name: power-of-two exponent
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The exponent $k \ge 0$ such that $2^k$ is the denominator of a dyadic rational $m/2^k$.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: A Gaussian dyadic number is a complex number $z = a + bi$ whose real part $a$ and imaginary part $b$ are both dyadic rationals, that is, rationals $m/2^k$ with $m$ an integer and $k \ge 0$.

gaussian-dyadic.name: Gaussian dyadic set
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The set of all Gaussian dyadic numbers.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: Write $\mathcal{G}$ for the set of these numbers.

gaussian-dyadic.name: butterfly map
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The map sending a pair $(u,v)$ to $((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2)$.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: The butterfly layer applies a map $H_0(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2)$ to pairs $u, v$ of values.

gaussian-dyadic.name: first butterfly input
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The first value of an input pair to the butterfly map $H_0$.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: The butterfly layer applies a map $H_0(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2)$ to pairs $u, v$ of values.

gaussian-dyadic.name: second butterfly input
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The second value of an input pair to the butterfly map $H_0$.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: The butterfly layer applies a map $H_0(u,v) = ((u+v)/2, (u-v)/2)$ to pairs $u, v$ of values.

gaussian-dyadic.name: fractional bit count
gaussian-dyadic.meaning: The number of fractional bits in each stored part, so every stored part is a multiple of $2^{-p}$.
gaussian-dyadic.quote: Each stored part is a multiple of $2^{-p}$, where $p$ is the number of fractional bits.

gaussian-resampling.name: source length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of coordinates of the source transform, the length of the input vectors.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform of a longer length $t$, keeping both coordinate permutations inside the transform identity.

gaussian-resampling.name: target length
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The number of coordinates of the longer target transform, a count of its coordinates.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](fourier-transform.md) of length $s$, the number of its coordinates, as a transform of a longer length $t$, keeping both coordinate permutations inside the transform identity.

gaussian-resampling.name: normalized transform
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The normalized transform of length q, applied to a vector of length q.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $F_q$ be the normalized transform of length $q$: $(F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}$.

gaussian-resampling.name: generic linear map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A linear map whose operator norm is taken; it is a contraction when its norm is at most 1.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Gaussian resampling is measured by the [Operator norm of a linear map](operator-norm.md), $\|L\|=\sup_{\|u\|\le1}\|Lu\|$, so a linear map $L$ is a *contraction* when $\|L\|\le1$.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian width
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The integer width of the Gaussian factors, at least 2.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Fix an integer width $\sigma\ge2$, the Gaussian width.

gaussian-resampling.name: resampling map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map from C^s to C^t given by the first Gaussian formula.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $K$ and $M$ map $\mathbb C^s$ to $\mathbb C^t$ by

gaussian-resampling.name: sampling map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map from C^s to C^t given by the second Gaussian formula.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $K$ and $M$ map $\mathbb C^s$ to $\mathbb C^t$ by

gaussian-resampling.name: source permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The coordinate permutation of the source vectors with entries u_{tj}.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with $v$ of length $t$ (here $v$ is new).

gaussian-resampling.name: target permutation
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The coordinate permutation of the target vectors with entries v_{-sk}.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with $v$ of length $t$ (here $v$ is new).

gaussian-resampling.name: target vector
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A vector of length t, the argument of the target permutation.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $P_s$ and $P_t$ be the coordinate permutations $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with $v$ of length $t$ (here $v$ is new).

gaussian-resampling.name: integer precision
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The integer precision of the arithmetic, the bound on the hypotheses of the theorem.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The hypotheses are $p>100$, $2\le\sigma<\sqrt p$, $s<t<2^p$ and $\theta>p/\sigma^4$, where $p$ is the integer precision and $\theta=t/s-1$.

gaussian-resampling.name: relative excess
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The ratio t/s minus one, the relative excess of the target length over the source length.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The hypotheses are $p>100$, $2\le\sigma<\sqrt p$, $s<t<2^p$ and $\theta>p/\sigma^4$, where $p$ is the integer precision and $\theta=t/s-1$.

gaussian-resampling.name: nearest integer
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The integer nearest tj/s, with ties rounded up.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\rho_j=\lfloor tj/s+\tfrac12\rfloor$ be the integer nearest $tj/s$, with ties rounded up.

gaussian-resampling.name: rounding offset
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The offset tj/s minus its nearest integer, with absolute value at most one half.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\delta_j=tj/s-\rho_j$, so $|\delta_j|\le\tfrac12$.

gaussian-resampling.name: selection map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map from C^t to C^s that copies coordinate rho_j into entry j.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\Lambda:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ select coordinate $\rho_j$, $(\Lambda v)_j=v_{\rho_j}$.

gaussian-resampling.name: Gaussian diagonal
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The diagonal map multiplying entry j by e^{pi sigma^2 delta_j^2}.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\Delta$ multiply entry $j$ by $e^{\pi\sigma^2\delta_j^2}$.

gaussian-resampling.name: compensated map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map Lambda M Delta from C^s to itself.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Let $\Gamma=\Lambda M\Delta$ be the map from $\mathbb C^s$ to itself.

gaussian-resampling.name: identity map
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.
gaussian-resampling.quote: The other terms form $((\Gamma-I)u)_j$, where $I$ is the identity map.

gaussian-resampling.name: exponent
gaussian-resampling.meaning: A positive integer with t equal to 2 to the power nu.
gaussian-resampling.quote: In the application $t=2^{\nu}$, where $\nu$ is a positive integer, so $F_t$ has power-of-two length.

gaussian-resampling.name: first contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map one half times K, a contraction.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Put $K_1=\tfrac12K$ and $K_2=2^{1-2\sigma^2}\Delta\Gamma^{-1}\Lambda$.

gaussian-resampling.name: second contraction
gaussian-resampling.meaning: The map 2 to the power 1 minus 2 sigma^2 times Delta Gamma^{-1} Lambda, a contraction.
gaussian-resampling.quote: Put $K_1=\tfrac12K$ and $K_2=2^{1-2\sigma^2}\Delta\Gamma^{-1}\Lambda$.

linear-network.name: first bank value
linear-network.meaning: The value of the first bank, held on one wire.
linear-network.quote: Let $x$ be the value of the first bank and $y$ the value of the second, each on one wire.

linear-network.name: second bank value
linear-network.meaning: The value of the second bank, held on one wire.
linear-network.quote: Let $x$ be the value of the first bank and $y$ the value of the second, each on one wire.

multidim-transform.name: number of axes
multidim-transform.meaning: The number of axes of the array, which counts the coordinates each entry is indexed by.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, and index them by $\ell = 1,\dots,d$.

multidim-transform.name: axis index
multidim-transform.meaning: The position of an axis, running from 1 to d.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $d$ be the number of axes, and index them by $\ell = 1,\dots,d$.

multidim-transform.name: axis length
multidim-transform.meaning: The number of entries along axis ℓ, a power of two.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $r_\ell$, a power of two, be the number of entries along axis $\ell$.

multidim-transform.name: input index
multidim-transform.meaning: The input index along axis ℓ, running over 0 to r_ℓ − 1.
multidim-transform.quote: For each axis, $j_\ell$ and $k_\ell$ are the input and output indices along it, both running over $0,\dots,r_\ell-1$.

multidim-transform.name: output index
multidim-transform.meaning: The output index along axis ℓ, running over 0 to r_ℓ − 1.
multidim-transform.quote: For each axis, $j_\ell$ and $k_\ell$ are the input and output indices along it, both running over $0,\dots,r_\ell-1$.

multidim-transform.name: input array
multidim-transform.meaning: The array whose entries A_{j_1…j_d} are the input to the transform.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $A$ be the input array, with entries $A_{j_1\cdots j_d}$, and $B$ the transformed array, with entries $B_{k_1\cdots k_d}$.

multidim-transform.name: transformed array
multidim-transform.meaning: The array whose entries B_{k_1…k_d} are the output of the transform.
multidim-transform.quote: Let $A$ be the input array, with entries $A_{j_1\cdots j_d}$, and $B$ the transformed array, with entries $B_{k_1\cdots k_d}$.

operator-norm.name: linear map
operator-norm.meaning: A linear map from one finite-dimensional complex vector space to another, whose operator norm is taken.
operator-norm.quote: Let $\Phi$ be a linear map from one finite-dimensional complex vector space to another, each with a chosen vector norm $\|\cdot\|$.

operator-norm.name: input vector
operator-norm.meaning: A vector in the domain of the linear map, over which the supremum defining the operator norm ranges.
operator-norm.quote: Write $\xi$ for a vector in the domain of $\Phi$.

operator-norm.name: second linear map

order-of-element.name: element
order-of-element.meaning: An element of the group whose order is taken; in the argument, the product $\prod_\eta y_\eta^{\mu_\eta}$.
order-of-element.quote: The order of an element $\gamma$ of a multiplicative group is the least positive integer $N$ with $\gamma^N=1$, when such $N$ exists.

order-of-element.meaning: The least positive integer with $\gamma^N=1$, which counts the distinct powers of $\gamma$ before the identity repeats.
order-of-element.quote: The order of an element $\gamma$ of a multiplicative group is the least positive integer $N$ with $\gamma^N=1$, when such $N$ exists.

order-of-element.name: number of lengths
order-of-element.meaning: The number of pairwise coprime lengths $s_1,\dots,s_\nu$ of the source, a count.
order-of-element.quote: Now let $\nu$ be the number of pairwise coprime lengths $s_1,\dots,s_\nu$ of the source, where $s_\eta$ is the $\eta$-th length, and let $S=\prod_\eta s_\eta$.

order-of-element.name: length
order-of-element.meaning: The $\eta$-th of the pairwise coprime lengths, a positive integer.
order-of-element.quote: Now let $\nu$ be the number of pairwise coprime lengths $s_1,\dots,s_\nu$ of the source, where $s_\eta$ is the $\eta$-th length, and let $S=\prod_\eta s_\eta$.

order-of-element.name: inverse of prefix product
order-of-element.meaning: The inverse, modulo $s_\eta$, of the product of the earlier lengths; it is coprime to $s_\eta$.

polynomial-ring.name: polynomial variable
polynomial-ring.meaning: The formal variable of the ring, whose powers act as roots of unity on the remaining axes.
polynomial-ring.quote: Here $y$ is the formal variable of the ring.

polynomial-ring.name: coefficient count
polynomial-ring.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, which is a power of two.
polynomial-ring.quote: Here $r$ is the number of complex coefficients in each polynomial record, which is a power of two.

polynomial-ring.name: coefficient index
polynomial-ring.meaning: The index of a coefficient, running from 0 to r-1.

polynomial-ring.name: coefficient
polynomial-ring.meaning: The complex coefficient of y^i in the coefficient list of an element of the ring.
polynomial-ring.quote: The entry $a_i$ of this list is the coefficient of $y^i$, a complex number.

polynomial-ring.name: shift count
polynomial-ring.meaning: The number of places a coefficient is shifted by multiplication with a power of y, with 0 <= h < r.
polynomial-ring.quote: Here $h$, with $0\le h<r$, is the number of places a coefficient is shifted; the letter $h$ changes meaning here.

quotient-ring.name: polynomial ring
quotient-ring.meaning: The ring of complex polynomials in the formal variables θ_1 to θ_M.
quotient-ring.quote: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the ring of complex polynomials in the formal variables $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_M$, where $M$ is the number of variables.

quotient-ring.name: formal variable
quotient-ring.meaning: A formal variable of the polynomial ring, indexed from 1 to M.
quotient-ring.quote: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the ring of complex polynomials in the formal variables $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_M$, where $M$ is the number of variables.

quotient-ring.name: variable count
quotient-ring.meaning: The number of formal variables θ_1 to θ_M.
quotient-ring.quote: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be the ring of complex polynomials in the formal variables $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_M$, where $M$ is the number of variables.

quotient-ring.name: relation
quotient-ring.meaning: The i-th relation, a polynomial in the polynomial ring that is set to zero in the quotient.
quotient-ring.quote: Let $f_1,\dots,f_K$ be polynomials in $\mathcal{P}$, the relations, where $K$ is the number of relations.

quotient-ring.name: relation count
quotient-ring.meaning: The number of relations f_1 to f_K.
quotient-ring.quote: Let $f_1,\dots,f_K$ be polynomials in $\mathcal{P}$, the relations, where $K$ is the number of relations.

quotient-ring.name: ideal of relations
quotient-ring.meaning: The ideal generated by the relations, the set of all sums of the relations multiplied by polynomials.
quotient-ring.quote: The ideal generated by the relations, $J$, is the set of all sums of the relations multiplied by arbitrary polynomials $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_K$:

quotient-ring.name: multiplier
quotient-ring.meaning: The polynomial multiplier of the i-th relation in a sum that belongs to the ideal.
quotient-ring.quote: The ideal generated by the relations, $J$, is the set of all sums of the relations multiplied by arbitrary polynomials $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_K$:

quotient-ring.name: polynomial
quotient-ring.meaning: A polynomial in the polynomial ring, identified with another when their difference lies in the ideal.
quotient-ring.quote: Two polynomials $\phi,\psi$ are identified when $\phi-\psi\in J$, and the class of $\phi$ is written $[\phi]$.

quotient-ring.name: polynomial
quotient-ring.meaning: A second polynomial in the polynomial ring, identified with another when their difference lies in the ideal.
quotient-ring.quote: Two polynomials $\phi,\psi$ are identified when $\phi-\psi\in J$, and the class of $\phi$ is written $[\phi]$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit width
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of bits in each radix digit, a count of bits.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Fix a digit width $\beta$, the number of bits in each radix digit.

radix-digit-convolution.name: exact-recovery digit width
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The digit width as the exact-recovery page names it; this page uses beta for the same width.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The exact-recovery page calls this width $b$, but this page writes $\beta$ throughout.

radix-digit-convolution.name: digit count
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The number of radix digits in each input, a count of digits.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $m = \lceil n/\beta \rceil$ be the number of digits in each input.

radix-digit-convolution.name: first input digit
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The $i$-th radix digit of the first input, a value in $\{0,\dots,2^\beta-1\}$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The digit $u_i$, for $0 \le i \le m-1$, is the $i$-th radix digit of the first input, and $v_i$ is the $i$-th radix digit of the second input, each in $\{0,\dots,2^\beta-1\}$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: second input digit
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The $i$-th radix digit of the second input, a value in $\{0,\dots,2^\beta-1\}$.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The digit $u_i$, for $0 \le i \le m-1$, is the $i$-th radix digit of the first input, and $v_i$ is the $i$-th radix digit of the second input, each in $\{0,\dots,2^\beta-1\}$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: formal variable
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: A formal variable whose powers mark the coefficient positions.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $t$ be a formal variable marking coefficient positions.

radix-digit-convolution.name: first digit polynomial
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The polynomial whose coefficients are the radix digits of the first input.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The polynomial $U(t)$ has the digits of the first input as coefficients, and $V(t)$ has those of the second: $U(t) = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} u_i t^i$ and $V(t) = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} v_i t^i$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: second digit polynomial
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The polynomial whose coefficients are the radix digits of the second input.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: The polynomial $U(t)$ has the digits of the first input as coefficients, and $V(t)$ has those of the second: $U(t) = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} u_i t^i$ and $V(t) = \sum_{i=0}^{m-1} v_i t^i$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: product polynomial
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The product $U(t)V(t)$, a polynomial whose value at $2^\beta$ is the integer product.
radix-digit-convolution.quote: Let $W(t) = U(t)V(t)$ be the product polynomial, so the integer product is $U(2^\beta)V(2^\beta) = W(2^\beta)$.

radix-digit-convolution.name: convolution coefficient
radix-digit-convolution.meaning: The $k$-th coefficient of $W$, the sum of $u_i v_j$ over $i+j=k$.

Take one coordinate of length $q$, so $\hat u_k=\frac1q\sum_j u_j\exp(-2\pi i jk/q)$.

Each product $\mu_j\nu_{(k-j)\bmod q}$ equals $\tau_k\,u_j\chi_j\overline{\chi_{k-j}}$: at a wrap the two sign changes cancel, and $\tau_j\tau_{k-j}=\tau_k$.
